source.title: Tracing the Path to Grokking: Dropout, Embeddings, and Network Activation

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure references and numbering appear inconsistent, but the relevant results are described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on modular addition and examines representation, initialization, and weight-decay effects using measurements and conditions that differ from a direct reproduction of the original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper's own modular-addition results are recorded below. Results attributed to other papers in the introduction and references are not included. Figure-only values are not estimated from plots. The paper does not vary training-set size.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own modular-addition MLP and reports delayed generalization. It tracks continuous indicators (embedding cosine structure, embedding distributions, dropout variance, sparsity) against the test-accuracy rise. It also varies initialization scale, initialization shift and weight decay, and reports their effect on the delay. Methods differ from the originals: an MLP rather than a transformer, no Fourier-circuit analysis, and no variation of dataset size.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that dropout variance, dropout robustness curves, embedding cosine patterns, weight/embedding distribution statistics and neuron activity all correlate with grokking onset and can help forecast it. They add that embeddings converge to a bimodal distribution regardless of initialization, reflecting dataset symmetries, so grokking stems from those symmetries rather than overtraining.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition, but specifies a two-layer MLP with a 256-neuron hidden layer, P=53, AdamW, weight decay of unity, learning rate 3x10-4, and a training fraction of 0.5. The original recipe is not described in this text, so exact procedural equivalence cannot be established.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale and profile, layer-specific initialization shifts, adding a ReLU layer after embeddings, dropout rate, weight decay, and number of neurons are reported to affect timing or measured outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Test-accuracy variance under MC dropout peaks around grokking onset, then falls to near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout-induced test-accuracy variance peaks during the memorization-to-generalization transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy becomes robust to dropout (unaffected below 0.2) once the model generalizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalized solutions are more robust to dropout perturbation than memorizing ones.

record.problems: The paper provides few numerical values for accuracy or timing beyond selected epochs and qualitative descriptions; several results are presented in figures without tabulated values. It tests one modular-addition setup and does not vary training-set size. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Figure/case numbering is inconsistent in the initialization discussion.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (the fraction is fixed at 0.5); other algorithmic tasks.
Identification of a Fourier or other generalizing circuit; removal of memorizing components.
Non-algorithmic data; switching grokking on/off; lazy-to-rich transition; explicit weight-norm control.
All; no LLM or realistic-data training.
Circuit efficiency comparison; critical dataset size; ungrokking.
All; optimizer and floating-point artifacts are not examined.

missing.what: Neuron sparsity time course: inactive neurons fall during memorization, then rise as symmetries are found. Proposed as a grokking predictor.
Std and mean of the embedding/weight distributions contract and shift early in training, proposed as a predictor; scaled init α=7 compared with unscaled.
Bimodal ±0.4 embedding distribution is independent of initialization scale and profile.
Embedding peak magnitude decreases with larger weight decay or fewer neurons per layer.
The [0.4,0.8] uniform shift gives a smaller delay than unshifted initialization; this is not recorded in R10.

record.verdict_notes: Single small MLP setup on modular addition P=53. Results are almost entirely qualitative or figure-only, with no uncertainty estimates. Case numbering in Sec. 3.3 is inconsistent. The init-scale result (R8) is on algorithmic data, so it supports only the init-scale part of V3. Record's limits_scope labels based on untested parts (V2 R6) were removed per rules.

versions.untested_parts: The effect of shrinking the training set on the delay is not tested.
The paper measures embedding structure and related indicators, but does not identify a Fourier algorithm or directly measure memorizing components being removed.
Initialization changes are tested on modular addition only; non-algorithmic datasets, weight-norm control, and a lazy-to-rich transition are not tested.
LLM pretraining and fine-tuning on realistic data.
The paper does not test an efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
Whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and floating-point or softmax artifacts are not investigated.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP with 256-neuron hidden layer and output size P=53
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and track training and test accuracy
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over epochs
rows.value: Training accuracy reaches its maximum after 300 epochs; test-accuracy growth begins around 450 epochs and reaches a maximum at 1200 epochs.
rows.note: The text describes training accuracy saturating before test accuracy rises. No numerical accuracy values are stated.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2; Section 3.2, paragraph preceding Figure 3; Figure 3 caption.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP with 256-neuron hidden layer and output size P=53
rows.operation_detail: Measure test-accuracy variance across 100 stochastic forward passes with dropout
rows.measure: Variance of test accuracy across stochastic dropout passes
rows.value: Variance is initially negligible while training accuracy rises to and stays at its maximum; it increases rapidly at the onset of generalization, then falls to near zero once train and test accuracy attain their maxima.
rows.note: This is a proposed diagnostic signal, not a direct measurement of the circuit or of the training-set-size relationship.
rows.check: Dropout variance is a stability diagnostic, not the grokking behaviour or a circuit measure. Kept under fits_no_version. Text says variance rises 'at the onset', not clearly before it.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP with 256-neuron hidden layer and output size P=53
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate test accuracy across dropout rates at selected training epochs
rows.measure: Test accuracy under different dropout rates
rows.baseline: Test accuracy at dropout rate 0.0; numerical value not stated
rows.value: At approximately 500 epochs test accuracy is close to zero across dropout rates. At 1000 epochs it starts to increase but is affected by small dropout rates. At approximately 1500 epochs it is largely unaffected below 0.2 and does not degrade substantially until dropout rate 0.5. At 2000 and 2500 epochs test accuracy has attained its maximum.
rows.note: The result concerns robustness of test accuracy to dropout, rather than the unperturbed accuracy curve alone.
rows.check: Dropout-robustness curve is a stability measure. Kept under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP with 256-neuron hidden layer and output size P=53
rows.operation_detail: Measure cosine similarity between embedding vectors
rows.value: Codiagonal patterns appear by 300 epochs; more discernible bands appear by 450 epochs, coinciding with the beginning of test-accuracy growth; the heatmap is structured when test accuracy reaches its maximum at 1200 epochs.
rows.note: The paper reports gradual representation structure preceding and accompanying generalization, but does not identify the claimed generalizing circuit.
rows.check: The anticipation part of V2 is shown: codiagonals appear at epoch 300, before the test rise at about 450. Fourier-circuit identification is untested, which should be listed as untested rather than downgrading the state.

rows.value: The distribution gradually develops two symmetric peaks centered around ±0.4; the paper says the peaks emerge concurrently with diagonal embedding patterns and the rise in test accuracy.
rows.note: A representation-level progress indicator is reported; circuit formation and removal of memorizing components are not directly measured.
rows.check: Peaks are described as emerging concurrently with the test-accuracy rise, not clearly before it.

rows.operation_detail: Keep embedding-layer weights constant during training
rows.measure: Embedding distribution, cosine-similarity structure, and grokking
rows.baseline: Trainable embedding weights; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: The embedding distribution remains Gaussian, the cosine-similarity heatmap remains unstructured, and grokking is suppressed.

rows.check: Freezing the embeddings keeps them unstructured and suppresses grokking. This is causal evidence that the emerging structure underlies generalization. The state should not be partial merely because the circuit is unidentified.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP with 256-neuron hidden layer and output size P=53
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy; embedding distribution
rows.baseline: Unshifted initialization; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: The embedding distribution shifts toward zero, becomes Gaussian as training accuracy starts to rise, then widens and forms two peaks before test accuracy increases.
rows.note: The test-accuracy timing is described qualitatively.
rows.check: The value describes the embedding distribution forming two peaks before the test rise, which is a progress measure (V2), not the V1 delay. Per the text, this case [0.4,0.8] also showed a smaller delay than unshifted; that is not recorded in the row.

rows.subject: Two-layer MLP with 256-neuron hidden layer and output size P=53
rows.baseline: Unshifted initialization; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: The delay before grokking is smaller than with the unshifted distribution.
rows.note: The text calls this one of the cases with a smaller delay; it gives no numerical timing.
rows.check: Grokking occurs with a smaller delay despite larger initial weight magnitudes. For V3 this shows mean-shifted (larger-norm) initialization shortening the delay, contrary to a simple scale/norm account.

source_check.correct: V1 state: observed; the paper reports grokking with a smaller delay for [1.2,1.6], without reporting a weakened endpoint. V3 state: cannot_determine; remove the V3 link because the condition does not test non-algorithmic grokking or an on/off transition.

source_check.problem: A shorter delay alone does not make V1 partial, and V3 does not assert monotonic growth of delay with initialization magnitude.

source_check.notes: The pack truncates several row values; the visible claims were checked against their source passages. The paper contains figure/case cross-reference errors and gives no numerical endpoint for [1.6,2]; its symmetry-based causal interpretation exceeds the diagnostics directly established.

statements.correction: Embedding-only and remaining-weight initialization shifts use normal distributions with mean 0.2 and standard deviation 0.1; both increase delay, with a stronger effect for remaining weights. Uniform shifts [1.2,1.6] shorten delay; [1.6,2] reduces test accuracy. No matched-total-norm comparison is reported.
statements.problem: The study shifts layer-specific initialization means; it does not isolate relative embedding scale at matched total norm or establish an effect beyond total norm.
